public_rationale: OpenAI's own documentation supports the concern about unreliable results and poorly communicated uncertainty. It also described concrete capabilities. Those facts do not settle whether ordinary users could anticipate successful execution across ChatGPT as a whole. The assertion that improvement would make it a different product has no measurable criterion. The complete claim therefore remains unresolved.
limitations: Evidence about one feature cannot establish the reliability of every ChatGPT model and use.
Documented features do not establish clear success boundaries.
Only original launch material is used; later updates on the live pages are excluded.
The product-identity clause is evaluative and is not independently scored.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: ChatGPT currently cannot be relied on to do what it's asked and its capabilities are unclear; a better ChatGPT would be a different product.

our_interpretation: Read the execution claim as saying users cannot generally assume successful completion without checking. Do not read it as saying ChatGPT never completes a request.
Read capability clarity as whether ordinary users can anticipate which requests will succeed, rather than merely whether feature documentation exists.
'A different product' is an evaluative description without a stated product-identity test or forecast deadline.
Use the current calendar year through publication, 2025-01-01 to 2025-06-09, as the reporting window for the ongoing state. Assess versions and features available during that window.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous product evaluations show consequential execution failures and poor communication of capability limits; user evidence shows that expected success boundaries are unclear.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evaluations show dependable execution within clearly communicated capabilities, and user evidence demonstrates that ordinary users can identify those boundaries.

evidence.explanation: OpenAI acknowledged both source-assessment failures and difficulty communicating uncertainty in ChatGPT's deep research feature. This supports the warning against assuming successful, trustworthy execution, but covers only one feature.

The launch documentation described concrete operations for models available within ChatGPT. Documentation is material context against total capability obscurity, but it does not show that users understood when those operations would succeed.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Contemporaneous tests of representative ChatGPT requests, paired with user studies of expected versus actual success. The product-identity clause would additionally need an operational definition.
